PSYCHIATRIC EMERGENCY SERVICE — EVALUATION
Date of service: 10/25/2024

Ms. Bianchi is a 49-year-old woman with recurrent severe major depression and temporal lobe epilepsy (neurology evaluation in 2020), Crohn's disease with short bowel syndrome on home TPN, brought in by her sister for a change in behavior over the last two weeks.

She has stayed shut in her apartment and will not go out. She is convinced the people next door can be heard through the walls talking about her sins, and she believes she is being punished by God for having failed as a mother. She cries much of the day, calls herself "unfixable," and says she belongs in jail. Eating little, waking very early, no energy. She has thoughts that she would be better off dead but no intention or plan to act on them.

Collateral (sister): several past depressive episodes, never one this bad. No history of mania, hypomania or psychosis.

Medications: she is not currently taking any psychiatric medication — she tells us she stopped her sertraline, bupropion and alprazolam on her own around August. Other: lamotrigine 100 mg twice daily from neurology, which she kept taking; diphenhydramine at night, multivitamin, TPN nightly, vedolizumab infusions every 8 weeks through GI.
Allergies/intolerances: NSAIDs, gabapentin.
Substances: none. Social: unemployed (disability), lives by herself.

Vital signs normal. Physical exam unremarkable.
Mental status: flat affect; avoids eye contact throughout. Mood-congruent delusions of guilt and persecution as above. No hallucinations reported. Cognitive screen without evidence of dementia; neurologic exam intact.
Urine drug screen negative.

Assessment: major depressive disorder, recurrent, severe, with psychotic features, in the setting of stopping her antidepressants. Passive death wish, lives alone, unable to care for herself safely.

Disposition: voluntary admission to the inpatient psychiatry unit.

INPATIENT PSYCHIATRY — DISCHARGE SUMMARY, regional hospital
Admitted 10/25/2024 — Discharged 11/12/2024 (voluntary)

Diagnosis: major depressive disorder, recurrent, severe, with psychotic features.

Course: Admitted after two weeks of worsening depression with delusions of guilt and persecution after she stopped her antidepressants on her own about two months earlier. Sertraline was restarted and brought back to 100 mg, bupropion XL 150 mg was resumed, and aripiprazole 5 mg daily was added for the psychotic features. She took part in groups and individual therapy. TPN continued nightly via her line with the home infusion formula. No seizures. By the second week the delusional thinking had receded; by discharge she was eating, sleeping through to morning, and denied any thoughts of death. Her sister was involved in family meetings and will check on her daily.

Discharge medications: sertraline 100 mg daily; bupropion XL 150 mg daily; aripiprazole 5 mg daily (new); alprazolam 0.25 mg as needed for anxiety, sparingly; diphenhydramine 25 mg at bedtime as needed; lamotrigine 100 mg twice daily (continued); multivitamin; TPN nightly; vedolizumab every 8 weeks with GI.
Allergies: NSAIDs, gabapentin.

Follow-up: outpatient psychiatry 12/09/2024; PCP within one week. Crisis resources provided.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with sister after inpatient psych 10/25–11/12 for recurrent MDD, severe, with psychotic features. Psych ED note and discharge summary reviewed. Med rec done with the bottles:
- sertraline 100 daily (restarted)
- bupropion XL 150 daily (restarted)
- aripiprazole 5 daily (new)
- alprazolam 0.25 prn (restarted; has used none since d/c)
- lamotrigine 100 bid (never stopped — neurology told her not to)
- diphenhydramine 25 qhs prn, MVI, TPN nightly, vedolizumab q8wk at GI

She says she stopped everything in August because she "felt fine and didn't want to be on pills forever," then slid fast. Now: sleeping, eating better, the "thoughts about the neighbors" are gone. Still low and tired. No thoughts of death or self-harm. Sister checks in daily, and they set up a pill organizer.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Weight 56.0, down almost 5 kg since July. Calm, soft-spoken, appropriate, no evident psychotic content. Line site clean.
PHQ-9 16, GAD-7 13.

A/P:
1. MDD, recurrent, severe with psychotic features — improving. Continue regimen; psych f/u 12/9. Safety plan reviewed; she and sister have crisis numbers.
2. Weight loss with the episode — will follow; GI/home infusion aware.
3. Missed flu shot this fall — trivalent flu and 2024–25 COVID given today.
4. Tobacco — still a few a week.
RTC 2 months, sooner prn.

Outpatient Psychiatry — follow-up after hospitalization, 12/09/2024

Ms. Bianchi returns four weeks after discharge from inpatient psychiatry for a psychotic depressive episode. She is taking sertraline 100 mg, bupropion XL 150 mg and aripiprazole 5 mg daily as prescribed; she has needed alprazolam only twice. Mood is low but improving; no delusional content elicited, no hallucinations, no thoughts of death. Sleep and appetite better.

Plan: no changes. Continue aripiprazole for at least several months, then reassess. Return in 6 weeks. We talked frankly about not stopping medication without a plan.

Outpatient Psychiatry

Symmetric T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the central pons with sparing of the peripheral pontine fibers, with corresponding restricted diffusion. No extrapontine signal abnormality; basal ganglia and thalami normal. No hemorrhage, mass or hydrocephalus. Hippocampi symmetric in size and signal. Remainder of the brain unremarkable for age.
reports.conclusion: Central pontine signal abnormality with restricted diffusion, consistent with central pontine myelinolysis (osmotic demyelination). No extrapontine involvement.

documents.title: Discharge Summary — Internal Medicine / ICU
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY — regional hospital, Internal Medicine (including ICU stay)
Admitted 11/07/2025 — Discharged 12/05/2025 to inpatient rehabilitation

Principal diagnoses: hyponatremia (SIADH); central pontine myelinolysis.
Other: Crohn's disease with short bowel syndrome on home TPN; temporal lobe epilepsy; recurrent major depressive disorder in partial remission; generalized anxiety disorder; history of provoked PE (2023); s/p cholecystectomy; chronic low back pain; right superior gluteal nerve palsy.

History: 50-year-old woman found confused and lethargic at home by her sister. Initial serum sodium 112 mEq/L. Former light smoker (stopped about three months ago, previously around a pack a week); social alcohol; on disability leave from administrative work.
Home medications: sertraline 100 mg, bupropion XL 150 mg, alprazolam 0.25 mg prn, diphenhydramine 25 mg qhs prn, lamotrigine 100 mg twice daily, multivitamin, TPN nightly, vedolizumab 300 mg IV every 8 weeks (an outside list also carried a combined OCP, which had been stopped in 2023).
Allergies: NSAIDs, gabapentin.

Course:
Hyponatremia — serum osmolality 238 mOsm/kg, urine osmolality 420 mOsm/kg, urine sodium 54 mEq/L, consistent with SIADH; sertraline considered a likely contributor and discontinued. She received intravenous saline. Over the following 48 hours her sodium rose to 129 mEq/L. Sodium normal by discharge.

Neurologic decline — on hospital day 3 (11/09) she became unresponsive and was moved to the ICU. Exam there: eyes open to painful stimulus, blinks on command, otherwise no movement; no speech; no limb movement; pupils reactive. Neurology consulted. MRI brain 11/12: central pontine T2/FLAIR change with restricted diffusion sparing the periphery, no extrapontine lesions — central pontine myelinolysis. Managed supportively; airway protected without intubation; aspiration precautions; nothing by mouth, with her TPN continued for nutrition. Bupropion was held while she could not swallow and resumed after a passed swallow evaluation. Lamotrigine 100 mg twice daily continued without interruption, crushed through a nasogastric tube while she could not swallow and by mouth afterward. Her vedolizumab infusion, due during the admission, was deferred to her GI team after rehabilitation. No seizures during the admission.
Over the following weeks eye movements, then limb movements and speech returned gradually. Transferred to the medical floor 11/21. At discharge she is moving all limbs, speaking with dysarthria, and requires assistance for transfers and walking.

Discharge medications: bupropion XL 150 mg daily; lamotrigine 100 mg twice daily; alprazolam 0.25 mg as needed for anxiety; diphenhydramine 25 mg at bedtime as needed; multivitamin; TPN nightly. Vedolizumab: next infusion with GI after rehabilitation. STOPPED: sertraline.

Disposition: acute inpatient rehabilitation. PCP and outpatient psychiatry to be updated; neurology follow-up after rehabilitation.

documents.author: PCP

Now opening eyes, following commands, beginning to move hands and say a few words. Swallow being reassessed. TPN continues via her line. Rehab planned once stable. I shared her history (TLE, psych admission 2024, PE 2023). Will see her after discharge. Called sister with update.

documents.title: Inpatient Rehabilitation Discharge Summary
documents.author: rehabilitation medicine
documents.body:
ACUTE INPATIENT REHABILITATION — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 12/05/2025 — Discharged 01/23/2026 to home

Rehabilitation diagnosis: central pontine myelinolysis following correction of hyponatremia (SIADH), November 2025.

Program: physical, occupational and speech therapy daily. TPN continued nightly through her tunneled line with home infusion coordinating the transition home.

Progress: Arrived needing assistance for transfers and walking, with dysarthric speech. Steady gains throughout. At discharge she walks with a single-point cane, is independent in self-care (dressing, bathing, toileting, setting up her own TPN with infusion nursing checks), and her speech is mildly dysarthric but fully understandable. Gait remains mildly unsteady. Cognition intact for daily tasks. Mood fair; no thoughts of self-harm.

Discharge medications: bupropion XL 150 mg daily; lamotrigine 100 mg twice daily; alprazolam 0.25 mg as needed; diphenhydramine 25 mg at bedtime as needed; multivitamin; TPN nightly. Vedolizumab to resume at her GI infusion center. Sertraline remains discontinued.
Allergies: NSAIDs, gabapentin.

Services: home health PT/OT, home infusion nursing. Her sister will stay with her the first week.
Follow-up: PCP within one week; outpatient neurology; outpatient psychiatry.
